title: The Turning Sky is out: a 44 track open world score, every place written for day and for night
body:
The Turning Sky is a 44 track exploration score for open world games. Twelve places are each written twice, once in daylight and once after dark, and both halves of a pair share a tonic and the same melodic cell. It is live now at $14.99, with 2 full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. A field is walked at noon and at midnight, and the player should know it is the same field. So the night version of each place is its day version in a different light: a darker mode, a slower tempo, the melody lower and passed to a different instrument played softer, and fewer notes. A check that reads the finished MIDI confirms, on all 12 pairs, the shared cell and that the night half is slower, lower in the melody, softer and thinner.

What is in it. The twelve places (The Open Field, The Deep Wood, The Long Shore, The River Road, The High Heath, The Mountain Road, The Wide Marsh, The Old Walls, The Upper Ridge, The Drowned Fen, The Whole Country and Out on the Water), a title theme and an overworld piece, six weather tracks, a camp, a map screen theme, a daybreak and 9 short cues. 35 full pieces and 53:10 of music. 35 tracks loop on sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags that RPG Maker reads directly, and the editable .mid ships beside every .ogg. It is an exploration record: there are no town, battle, boss or dungeon tracks in it.

How it was checked. 782 theory checks and 501 audio checks, 0 failed, with both reports inside the download. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free pair (The Open Field and The Field After Dark) is for: one place at both ends of the day.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.

https://csaf.itch.io/the-turning-sky
